description: Matched local mechanism-removal experiments. Baseline and variant use identical recovery episode specifications; failure outcomes are measured, not manufactured in the oracle.

pairs.hypothesis: Changing the key after a lost partial-refund response can create a second effect when sufficient balance remains.
Changing the key after a lost full-refund response may fail recovery even when provider balance constraints prevent a duplicate effect.
Treating a returned refund ID as success can report a pending refund as verified before a monetary effect exists.
Treating a returned refund ID as success can falsely verify a failed refund, including subsequent cached responses.
